facts.text: La Bohème premiered on 1 February 1896 at the Teatro Regio in Turin, conducted by the 28-year-old Arturo Toscanini.
The first-night audience was subdued, and the critics were divided.
facts.evidence: The initial response of the audience at the first performance was subdued and critical responses were polarized.

facts.text: Toscanini conducted it again on radio in 1946, 50 years after the premiere. It is the only recording of a Puccini opera by its original conductor.
evidence: In 1946, 50 years after the opera's premiere, Toscanini conducted a commemorative performance
It is the only recording ever made of a Puccini opera by its original conductor.

facts.text: Ruggero Leoncavallo claimed he had offered Puccini a finished Bohème libretto. Puccini said he hadn't known and wouldn't abandon his own opera, so Leoncavallo wrote a rival Bohème.
evidence: who said that he had offered Puccini a completed libretto
he felt that he could not oblige him by abandoning the opera

facts.text: Leoncavallo’s rival version swapped the voices: his Marcello is a tenor and his Rodolfo a baritone.
facts.evidence: Leoncavallo completed his own version in which Marcello was sung by a tenor and Rodolfo by a baritone.

facts.text: “Che gelida manina” was recorded by nearly 500 tenors in at least seven languages between 1900 and 1980.
facts.evidence: This aria has been recorded by nearly 500 tenors in at least seven different languages between 1900 and 1980.

facts.text: Enrico Caruso, closely associated with Rodolfo, recorded this aria in 1906.
facts.evidence: Enrico Caruso, who was closely associated with the role of Rodolfo, recorded the famous aria "Che gelida manina" in 1906.

facts.text: Rodolfo turns to see Mimì bathed in moonlight, and their voices join in “O soave fanciulla”.

facts.text: Act II opens at the Café Momus with a big crowd, children included, and street sellers calling out their wares.

facts.text: In this quartet, Mimì and Rodolfo part tenderly while Marcello and Musetta quarrel fiercely about her flirting.

facts.text: When news of Puccini’s death reached Rome in 1924, a Bohème performance was stopped and the orchestra played Chopin’s Funeral March.
evidence: the news of his death reached Rome during a performance of La bohème
The opera was immediately stopped, and the orchestra played Chopin's Funeral March for the stunned audience.

facts.text: The Met first staged La Bohème on 26 December 1900, with Nellie Melba as Mimì.
facts.evidence: The Metropolitan Opera staged the work for the first time on 26 December 1900 with Nellie Melba as Mimì

facts.text: La Bohème was the last opera performed in the Met’s original 1883 building, on 16 April 1966.
facts.evidence: La bohème was the last opera performed at New York's Metropolitan Opera's original 1883 building on 16 April 1966

facts.text: Benjamin Britten wrote in 1951 that after four or five performances he never wanted to hear Bohème again.
